History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
• 25-year-old woman with 2-day history of constant dull lower-abdominal ache, nausea, and subjective fever/diaphoresis; no vomiting. Seeks evaluation and relief; GP advised face-to-face assessment and pregnancy rule-out.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant dull aching pain below the umbilicus associated with nausea and feeling hot/sweaty for the past 2–3 days.  
• Onset & progression: Gradual onset two days ago; symptoms persist and are becoming uncomfortable.  
• Gastrointestinal: No vomiting. Constipation one week ago, now resolved; last bowel movement yesterday; currently passing stools normally. No diarrhoea.  
• Genitourinary: ↑ urinary frequency; no dysuria, urgency, malodour, or pelvic/vaginal discharge. Noted slight pink tinge in urine over the last few days; patient is due for period (LMP ≈ 3+ weeks ago).  
• Gynaecological: Sexually active with one partner; uses contraceptive implant (Implanon). Unsure about pregnancy but believes risk is low. No vaginal discharge.  
• Constitutional: Subjective fever, hot/sweaty. No light-headedness, presyncope, or fainting reported.  
• Review of systems: No other system complaints reported.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Allergies: Amoxicillin – reaction details not documented.  
• Medications: 
  – Contraceptive implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented (long-acting subdermal device).

Social History:
• Lives with boyfriend.  
• Denies smoking.  
• Drinks “lots of water”; alcohol and other substances not discussed.

Family History:
• Brother: Type 1 diabetes mellitus.  
• No other familial diseases noted.

Physical Examination:
• No physical examination performed during tele-consult.  
• Vitals not recorded.

Investigations:
• None performed during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Lower-abdominal pain with nausea ± constitutional symptoms
  • Assessment: Differential includes constipation, urinary tract pathology, early pregnancy/ectopic, gynaecologic causes.  
  • Plan:
    – Arrange same-day face-to-face GP appointment for abdominal and pelvic examination.  
    – Perform urine pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy/ectopic.  
    – Consider urine dipstick, urinalysis, serum β-hCG, FBC, CRP, abdominal/pelvic imaging as indicated after exam.  
    – Provide safety-net advice: If pain worsens, develops light-headedness, vomiting, heavy bleeding, or other concerning symptoms, seek urgent medical attention or ED review.

Issue 2: Subjective fever/diaphoresis
  • Assessment: Could be associated with underlying abdominal/GU pathology.  
  • Plan:
    – Record temperature and full vitals at face-to-face visit.  
    – Treat underlying cause once identified.

General Plan Items:
• Review results promptly and follow-up clinically after investigations.  
• Document allergy to Amoxicillin in records.  
• Provide patient education on recognising red-flag symptoms.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: vitals, physical examination findings, full medication list (OTC/supplements), complete allergy details (reaction type), alcohol intake.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational overlap but clinically adequate.
